title: prefill-sampler-and-quant-sentinel-autotune
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token cost by combining a lightweight prefill-sampler (shape-aware cold prefetch) with a staged quantization sentinel that safely expands aggressive quant profiles only where unit economics and quality tolerances are met. This PR implements an autotune path that: 1) observes real request length/shape distributions via a streaming sampler, 2) computes candidate batch/cache/quant presets for 'cold' and 'steady' windows, 3) deploys candidates to a shadow canary, and 4) promotes profiles when end-to-end unit-econ and quality signals pass thresholds.

This change spans runtime, planner, and ops tooling: runtime gets a non-blocking prefill-sampler that records sequence shape histograms and pre-warms KV caches for long-tail prefixes; the planner receives a new PrefillSamplerProfile and shape-aware batch templates; the quant service introduces the QuantSentinel which runs compact A/B tests with low-latency trials and enforces rollback on quality regressions. The CLI (rwd-econ) and console pages surface suggested profiles and a single-click promote/rollback flow.

Checklist:
- [x] implement prefill sampler and histogram collector
- [x] add planner heuristics for shape-aware batching templates
- [x] implement QuantSentinel with canary, shadow and rollback hooks
- [x] CLI + Console integration for profile suggestions and promotions
- [x] unit + integration tests for safety guards
- [x] perf benchmarks and smoke tests against common workloads

Impact summary: In internal synthetic workloads and three customer traces (chat, summarization, retrieval-augmented QA) default automated runs show 8–18% token cost reduction with median latency impact <5ms and observed quality delta within configured thresholds (ROUGE/acceptance tests). The autotune flow is conservative by default (dry-run for first 48h), and operators can opt into faster promotion windows.

Related: Linked Linear items and notes in the ticket; follows design from ENG-4183 and is complementary to existing econ-prescriptor logic. This is intended as an iterative step toward making default batching/quant presets a dynamic, workload-driven property rather than a static config file.

review_conversation: Ethan Park (reviewer): The sentinel rollback path looks good but ensure that the rollback decision uses a rolling window rather than a single failing trial. Also add an explainable metric in logs for why a profile failed.
Maya Chen (author): Added rolling-window evaluation (configurable via quant.sentinel.window) and a human-readable failure_reason field in the audit log. See commit e4f8a92.

Sofia Martinez (reviewer): Planner change looks fine; one nit about the batch template naming (use 'shape-<bucket>' to make dashboards readable). Consider a toggle to disable prefill warmup for memory-constrained hosts.
Maya Chen (author): Updated naming convention and added an opt-out flag prefill.disable_on_low_memory. See commit b77d3a8.
Noah Patel (approver): Verified perf numbers on canary cluster and reviewed safety tests. Approving with the expectation that we monitor cost regressions in the first week after rollout.
SRE Bot: Observability checks passed, canary metrics within thresholds for first 24h.
QA: Integration tests flaked once in CI on macOS runner, reran and passed.
release_notes: Add a prefill-sampler and QuantSentinel to enable workload-driven batching and quantization presets. Ships conservative autotune flow with dry-run by default. Expect 8-18% cost reductions on targeted workloads; operators can promote/rollback via console or rwd-econ CLI.
notes_for_ops: Default deployment leaves autotune in dry-run for 48h. To enable automatic promotions set quant.sentinel.auto_promote=true in the econ config and ensure audit retention for 7 days. Monitor econ.unit_cost and quality.acceptance_rate dashboards after enabling.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: changes are gated behind the sentinel and default to dry-run. Fallbacks are implemented for canary failures and cold prefill is opt-out. Quant aggressiveness is limited by safety thresholds and rollback hooks.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover sampler, planner heuristics, and sentinel controller. Integration test runs simulate trace replays for chat, summarization, and RAG. Perf smoke tests run across p3 and a100-backed clusters to validate latency regressions (<5ms median) and verify throughput stability.
deployment_instructions: Rollout plan: 1) deploy runtime and planner changes to staging; 2) enable prefill sampler (dry-run) on canary fleet; 3) start QuantSentinel in shadow mode and observe candidate trials for 48h; 4) review suggested profiles in console and promote manually or flip auto_promote; 5) monitor dashboards and metrics for 72h before broad rollout.
